content_html:
Huaraz, located in the Áncash region, is one of the most impressive destinations in Peru for lovers of trekking and nature. Surrounded by the majestic mountains of the Cordillera Blanca, this city is the perfect starting point to explore turquoise lakes, glaciers, and unique landscapes in the Andes.

The area is part of Huascarán National Park, a protected natural area recognized for its biodiversity and for hosting some of the highest mountains in Peru.

Must-Visit Lakes in the Cordillera Blanca

Laguna 69

Laguna 69 is one of the most famous hikes in Huaraz. Its turquoise waters surrounded by snow-capped mountains create one of the most spectacular landscapes in Peru.

  • Approximate altitude: 4,600 m (15,090 ft)
  • Trekking duration: 5 to 6 hours
  • Level: Moderate

Laguna Parón

Laguna Parón is the largest lake in the Cordillera Blanca and one of the most visited. From its viewpoints you can admire impressive snow-capped peaks such as Artesonraju.

Laguna Churup

Laguna Churup is another popular route for travelers looking for a challenging hike with incredible views.

  • Altitude: 4,450 m (14,600 ft)
  • Trekking duration: 3 to 4 hours
  • Level: Moderate

Best Time to Visit

The best season for trekking in Huaraz is between May and September, when the weather is drier and the skies are usually clear, allowing you to fully enjoy the landscapes of the Cordillera Blanca.

Travel Recommendations

Acclimatize for at least one day before hiking
Bring mountain clothing and sunscreen
Wear proper trekking shoes
Stay hydrated during hikes
